policy_decision.text: The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1 to 1-1/4 percent.

citations.quotation: the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1 to 1-1/4 percent

dissent.text: Neel Kashkari dissented, preferring to maintain the existing target range rather than raise it.

citations.quotation: Voting against the action was Neel Kashkari, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the existing target range for the federal funds rate

uncertainty.text: The statement notes near-term risks appear roughly balanced, but the Committee is closely monitoring inflation, which is running below its 2 percent objective—an uncertainty relevant to the future policy path.

citations.quotation: Near-term risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced, but the Committee is monitoring inflation developments closely.
Inflation on a 12-month basis is expected to remain somewhat below 2 percent in the near term but to stabilize around the Committee’s 2 percent objective over the medium term.

counterarguments.text: A counterpoint to reading the rate hike as a sign of a steady tightening path: the statement frames policy as still accommodative and contingent on inflation returning to 2 percent, which could support a more patient pace than a mechanical hike sequence implies.

citations.quotation: The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting some further strengthening in labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation.

limitations: The supplied excerpts are partial; the full statement, including the implementation directive details, is truncated.
The excerpts do not include the Committee's statement of Kashkari's reasoning, so his rationale cannot be characterized beyond his stated preference to hold the existing target range.
